tests.title: IELTS Reading Mock 1
tests.passage:
A US perspective on the development of the frozen food industry.

At some point in history, humans discovered that ice preserved food. Two thousand years ago, the inhabitants of South America's Andean mountains conserved potatoes by freezing them overnight, trampling them to squeeze out moisture, then drying them in the sun.

Natural ice remained the main form of refrigeration until late in the 19th century. In 1851, railroads began putting blocks of ice in insulated rail cars to send butter from Ogdensburg, New York, to Boston.

In 1870, Australian inventors found a way to make mechanical ice. Cattlemen realized this invention could export meat across oceans. In 1880, Australian beef and mutton was sent frozen to England, although crystals could spoil flavor and texture.

The modern frozen food industry began after Clarence Birdseye observed Inuit quick-freezing fish in Arctic air. Birdseye later developed mechanical freezers, quick-freezing techniques, packaging products in cellophane, and convenient consumer-sized packs.

Sales increased in the early 1940s when World War II made tin scarce for canned food. By the 1950s, refrigerator technology had become affordable, and millions of US families owned refrigerators. Swanson launched the TV Dinner in 1954 with a clever name and huge advertising budget.

answers.Part 1: Interview: I am a student. I enjoy English because it helps me communicate with more people. I usually prepare for exams by reviewing vocabulary and practising timed tasks.
answers.Part 2: Cue Card: A useful skill I learned is organizing my study time. I learned it last year when I had several exams close together. I used a weekly plan and divided large tasks into smaller goals. This skill is useful because it reduces stress and helps me finish important work on time.
answers.Part 3: Discussion: Young people need communication, problem solving and digital skills. Technology has made learning more flexible, but students still need discipline. Schools should teach practical skills because they prepare students for real life.

submissions.task1Answer: The line graph compares the proportion of people using five communication methods between 1998 and 2008. Overall, cellular phone service rose dramatically and became the most common method by the end of the period, while landline use remained relatively stable. Internet service also increased steadily, and both types of broadband appeared later and grew slowly. In 1998, landline service was used by about 15 percent of people, compared with only around 6 percent for cellular phones and 4 percent for internet service. By 2002, cellular use had overtaken landlines. It then climbed sharply to reach 60 percent in 2008. Internet service increased from about 4 percent to nearly 18 percent. Fixed and mobile broadband were almost unused until 2002, but both rose gradually to around 5 percent and 4 percent respectively by 2008.
submissions.task2Answer: I agree to a large extent that products with high sugar content should be made more expensive, because price is one of the strongest influences on consumer behaviour. If sugary drinks and snacks cost more, many people, especially young consumers, may buy them less often and choose healthier alternatives. This could reduce obesity, diabetes and other health problems over time. However, higher prices alone are not enough. Governments should also require clearer labels, limit advertising aimed at children and support affordable healthy food. Otherwise, the policy may unfairly affect low-income families without changing habits permanently. Therefore, making sugary products more expensive can be useful, but it should be combined with education and wider public health measures.
